YOUR WORKING DIRECTORY IS `/opt/nxeon-agent-p2` (git worktree, branch agent/hosting-p2) of the Nxeon shared-hosting platform (Next.js 15 + Tailwind + Prisma + a Node worker that SSHes hosting nodes for nginx/certbot/wp-cli). Do ALL work there. NEVER touch /opt/nxeon (live prod) or other /opt/nxeon-* worktrees. `cd /opt/nxeon-agent-p2` first. node_modules symlinked; tsc/build work.

# DESIGN SYSTEM RULES (non-negotiable — past work was rejected as "AI slop")
NO EMOJIS. Use `components/ui/Icon.tsx` (inline-SVG `<Icon>` set) + `components/ui/AppLogo.tsx`. Use `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + global `.card`/`.btn-*`/`.input` utilities. Geist fonts (don't set font-family; mono only for hostnames/paths). Match the existing hosting console (`components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx`).

# TASKS — 4 items on the hosting customer console

## 1. Remove the DUPLICATE usage section
The plan Overview currently shows usage TWICE: (a) the top row of resource stat-cards (Websites / Storage / Mailboxes / Databases / Backups) — KEEP THESE, the user likes them best; and (b) a lower "Resource usage" section with tiles (Storage / Inodes / Extra Sites / Databases) — REMOVE this lower section. Don't lose the one genuinely-unique metric there — **Inodes (files)** — fold it into the top cards (either a small "Files: 47,200" sub-line on the Storage card, or a compact Inodes card). No metric shown in two places.

## 2. Animated usage bars/graphs
The kept stat-cards with a quota (Storage, Websites, Mailboxes, Databases) should have a smooth **animated progress bar** that fills from 0 → its value on mount (CSS width/transform transition, ~600-900ms ease). On-brand violet→cyan gradient fill. Add a tasteful touch where it helps (e.g. a subtle sparkline is optional, not required). RESPECT `prefers-reduced-motion` (no animation → show final state). Keep it classy, not busy.

## 3. Smaller website cards — 3-4 per row
The website grid is currently ~2 big cards per row. Make the cards more COMPACT so 3-4 fit per row on desktop (grid `minmax(~240-260px, 1fr)`), with a smaller preview/thumbnail and tighter footer — while staying clean, clickable, and on-brand. Keep the status/app badges, hostname, Manage + kebab, and the "Add new website" card.

## 4. Build the DOMAIN-ATTACH gap (the important one)
The missing keystone: a customer who started on a free subdomain must be able to attach a REAL domain to their EXISTING website (same docroot/files) and make it the primary address — WITHOUT creating a new empty site. Today `createAddonDomain` spins up a separate empty docroot; there's no "point this domain at my existing site."

Build it on the website's **Domain & SSL** tab (§3.3):
- **Connect a domain** (a domain they own → DNS wizard showing the A record) and **Buy a domain** (link to the existing Namecheap register flow `/dashboard/domains/register`), that ATTACH the domain to THIS website — i.e. add the hostname as an additional `server_name` on THIS website's existing vhost/docroot, not a new one.
- **Make primary**: promote the attached domain to this website's primary address — regenerate the website's vhost with the new domain (keep the old free subdomain as an alias/redirect so nothing breaks), reissue/expand SSL, and if WordPress is detected in the docroot run `wp search-replace <old> <new>` + update home/siteurl.
- REUSE existing infra: `renderHostingVhost` already accepts alias server-names; `setPrimaryHostingDomain` + the `SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN` worker task + `primaryAliasesFor` + the WP-rewrite logic exist (from earlier work) — extend/generalize them for "attach + set-primary for a website" rather than only "promote an addon to account-primary." Add a clean action (e.g. `attachDomainToWebsite` / `setWebsitePrimaryDomain`) + wire the UI.
- Cross-tenant hostname claims must be honored (atomic UNIQUE(hostname), see `isHostnameClaimed`/`normalizeClaimHostname`). Back-compat: existing sites/domains unaffected. SANDBOX (non-prod) mocks the node — make the DB side testable in sandbox + the real node path worst-case-safe (old subdomain keeps serving if anything fails). This can only be fully validated on a real node — note that.

## HARD REQUIREMENTS
- Preserve every existing feature + ownership/security guard.
- Real data/actions only. Don't touch the VPS deploy wizard or non-hosting code.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. After any schema change: `npx prisma generate` first (avoid schema changes if you can).
- FULL build MUST pass: `export $(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon-staging/.env | xargs) && npm run build` → "Compiled successfully" + all pages generated, exit 0 (a sync export in a 'use server' file fails the build — keep actions async).
- `npx tsx --test test/hosting.test.ts` → no NEW failures (pre-existing `fpm pool` fail is fine).
- Emoji scan clean: `grep -rP "[\x{1F000}-\x{1FAFF}]" components/customer/hosting`.
- Do NOT touch `app/(marketing)` pricing files — I'm editing those in parallel.

## DELIVERABLE
Commit to agent/hosting-p2 (clear message). Do NOT push/deploy. Report: how you merged the usage sections, the animated bars, the new compact grid (cols per row), and — in detail — how the domain-attach + make-primary flow works (the new action(s), vhost/SSL/WP-rewrite behavior, back-compat, real-node caveat). Confirm tsc + full build + tests + emoji-clean. List shared-file edits.

content.text:
Committed to `agent/hosting-p2` (`ca36d1a`), not pushed. Here is the report.

## What was done

All four tasks completed on the customer hosting console. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, full build exits 0 with all pages generated, hosting unit tests pass (my new test included; only the pre-existing `fpm pool` test still fails), emoji scan clean.

### 1. Merged the duplicate usage sections
Removed the lower "Resource usage" card (`ResourceUsageCard`) entirely. Kept the top resource stat-cards (the ones the user prefers). The single unique metric there — **Inodes** — is folded onto the **Storage** card as a `Files: 47,200` sub-line. No metric is shown in two places. Also removed the now-unused `QuotaTile`/`fmtBytes` imports.

### 2. Animated usage bars
New local `QuotaStatCard` + `UsageBar` components mirror the shared `StatCard` styling and add a progress bar that animates width `0 → value` on mount (~750ms ease, `requestAnimationFrame` trigger). Fill is an on-brand `from-brand-400 to-accent-cyan` (violet→cyan) gradient, flipping amber at 100%. Bars appear on the four quota cards: **Websites, Storage, Mailboxes, Databases** (Backups has no quota, stays a plain `StatCard`). Honors `prefers-reduced-motion` via a `matchMedia` check that sets the final width immediately plus `motion-reduce:transition-none`.

### 3. Compact website grid — 3–4 per row
Grid changed from `sm:grid-cols-2` to `[grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(244px,1fr))]` → 3–4 cards/row on desktop. `WebsiteCard` tightened: app badge 40→32px, padding reduced, the two footer rows condensed into one `HTTPS · app · type` meta line, smaller add-new card (`min-h` 220→168px). Thumbnail, status/app badges, hostname link, Manage + kebab menu, and the "Add new website" card all preserved.

### 4. Domain-attach + make-primary (the keystone)
Built on the main website's **Domain & SSL** tab as a new `ConnectDomainCard` (rendered only for `site.kind === "primary"` — the site a free-subdomain-start customer already owns, whose `primaryDomain` may itself be a free subdomain). It offers **Connect a domain** (a domain they own, with the A-record DNS hint), **Buy a domain** (links to `/dashboard/domains/register`), a live **Domains on this website** list, and per-domain **Make primary**.

**New actions (`lib/actions-hosting.ts`):**
- `attachDomainToWebsite(accountId, siteRef, domain)` — registers the domain as an additional **PRIMARY-kind `HostingHostnameClaim`** inside a Serializable tx (the atomic `UNIQUE(hostname)` is the real cross-tenant guard; `isHostnameClaimed` is the advisory pre-check). Because `primaryAliasesFor` reads PRIMARY claims, the domain folds into the **existing** primary vhost's `server_name` as an alias — same docroot/files, no new empty site, no `maxSites` consumed. Queues a `SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN` task in `attachDomain` mode.
- `setWebsitePrimaryDomain(accountId, siteRef, domain)` — requires the domain to already be an owned PRIMARY claim, refuses if a primary-domain change is in flight, queues `SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN` in `makePrimaryDomain` mode. Owner/admin guard + `assertNotImpersonating`, DB flip deferred to the worker.
- `listAttachedDomains(accountId)` — the account's primary plus every PRIMARY-kind alias claim.

**Worker (`worker/hosting.ts`):** generalized `taskSetPrimaryDomain` into a dispatcher over three payload modes — `attachDomain` → `attachPrimaryAlias`, `makePrimaryDomain` → `promotePrimaryDomain(…, null)`, legacy `addonId` → `promotePrimaryDomain(…, addon)` (unchanged addon-promote behavior). Shared helpers:
- `attachPrimaryAlias` reinstalls `hosting-<user>.conf` with the new alias folded in (via `primaryAliasesFor` + `renderHostingVhost` aliases) and best-effort `certbot --expand`s the real cert when one exists and DNS is pointed (`--allow-subset-of-names --keep-until-expiring` → no-op, never an error, if unpointed).
- `promotePrimaryDomain` repoints the vhost onto the new domain keeping the old as an alias, tears down the addon's own vhost (addon path only), runs `wp search-replace` + `home/siteurl` when WordPress is detected in `public_html`, then flips `primaryDomain` / re-keys the claim.
- `primaryVhostSsl` never downgrades a live cert (prefers per-domain LE, then wildcard, then self-signed) so `nginx -t` can't fail on a missing file.

**Back-compat / safety:** no schema change (reuses `HostingHostnameClaim` + the existing `SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN` enum value — important because `node_modules` is a symlink to a shared tree, so `prisma generate` was deliberately avoided). Existing addon-promote (`setPrimaryHostingDomain`) is untouched. All node work throws **before** any DB flip, so the old address keeps serving on failure. The SANDBOX task sweep mirrors all three modes so the DB side is testable without a node. Cross-tenant claims honored via the atomic `UNIQUE(hostname)`.

**Pure/testable:** extracted `hostingServerNames(primary, aliases)` into `lib/hosting.ts` (re-validates + de-dupes www variants; `renderHostingVhost` now calls it) with a new unit test.

**Real-node caveat:** the certbot expand / vhost reload paths can only be fully validated on a live hosting node — sandbox mocks the node.

## Shared-file edits
- `lib/hosting.ts` — added `hostingServerNames` (additive, pure).
- `worker/hosting.ts` — generalized the SET_PRIMARY_DOMAIN worker task + sandbox sweep; `renderHostingVhost` now uses `hostingServerNames`.
- `lib/actions-hosting.ts` — 3 new exported actions + `AttachedDomainView` type.
- `test/hosting.test.ts` — new `hostingServerNames` test.

Did not touch `app/(marketing)` pricing files, the VPS deploy wizard, or any non-hosting code.
